question: Your patient is going home tomorrow and looks sad about saying goodbye to the ward staff. Which phase of the relationship are you in?

options.A: Termination phase
options.B: Working phase
options.C: Orientation phase
options.D: Assessment phase

explanation: Saying goodbye and wrapping up care is always part of the final termination phase. It's totally normal for patients to feel a bit sad! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h3)

question: A patient with a new forearm cast says the rough edge of the plaster is scratching their wrist. What should have been done with the stockinette to prevent this?

options.A: Stretching the stockinette tighter across the fingers
options.B: Soaking the outer stockinette in warm saline
options.C: Folding the stockinette edges back over the cast ends
options.D: Applying adhesive tape over the outer plaster

explanation: Rolling the extra stockinette material back over the edges of the hardened cast creates a smooth, protective border that stops skin irritation. You've got this! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T6#GNS221_U1_T6_h2)

question: Why are IV fluids given to a patient with a severe crush injury before they are freed?

options.A: To prevent external skin infections
options.B: To numb the pain of broken bones
options.C: To make the patient sleep through the rescue
options.D: To flush out toxins and protect the kidneys

explanation: That's right! Pumping in fluids helps dilute and flush those nasty muscle toxins through the kidneys safely before they can cause severe damage. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h5)

question: What is the best approach when a nurse gives dietary advice to a patient with a chronic condition?

options.A: Telling the patient to rely entirely on vitamin supplements instead of food
options.B: Focusing solely on what foods the patient must completely ban from the house
options.C: Tailoring advice to fit the patient's cultural background, finances, and lifestyle
options.D: Handing out a strict, pre-printed meal plan that cannot be changed

explanation: Spot on! Advice only works if it fits into the patient's real life, budget, and cultural preferences. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h7)

question: You are assessing a patient's abdomen and suspect peritonitis. Which physical sign would you expect to find?

options.A: A rigid, board-like abdomen
options.B: A soft, painless belly
options.C: Cool and moist skin on the arms
options.D: Increased bowel sounds everywhere

explanation: Brilliant! When the lining of the belly gets irritated by leaked digestive juices or stool, the muscle wall tightens up stiffly to protect itself. You're building solid assessment skills! [learn more](GNS213_U3_T14#GNS213_U3_T14_h4)

question: Why do mental health diagnostic manuals keep getting updated?

options.A: To make nursing documentation twice as long to complete
options.B: To reflect new research and changing scientific understanding
options.C: To increase the total number of medications manufacturers sell
options.D: To erase all past history of psychiatric care

explanation: Science never stops growing! As we discover more about the human mind, manuals are updated so your nursing care stays top-notch. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T3#GNS314_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the safest way to move a heavy patient up in bed without hurting your back?

options.A: Twist your torso to shift the weight in a single smooth motion
options.B: Ask the patient to push with their legs while you lift alone
options.C: Bend sharply at the waist to pull the patient quickly
options.D: Use an overhead mechanical lift and get a second staff member

explanation: Spot on! Protect your back by using mechanical tools and asking a colleague for help. Nursing is teamwork! [learn more](GST319_U4_T7#GST319_U4_T7_h4)

question: What is the main goal of taking anti-seizure medications?

options.A: To prevent future seizures by stabilizing brain activity
options.B: To permanently cure the underlying cause of epilepsy
options.C: To increase the speed of brain electrical signals
options.D: To immediately stop pain during a headache

explanation: These meds act like a steady anchor for the brain, calming down hyperactive nerve cells so seizures don't catch the patient off guard. You've got this concept down! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T11#GNS222_U4_T11_h7)

question: Which condition features flashbacks, avoiding reminders, and being constantly on edge long after a disaster?

options.A: Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder
options.B: Normal developmental grief
options.C: Acute bronchitis
options.D: Generalized physical fatigue

explanation: Spot on! PTSD is a long-lasting condition where individuals struggle with intrusive memories, avoidance, and a constant 'fight-or-flight' feeling after trauma. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h6)

question: Why is nurse-led advocacy essential for the prevention of mental health disorders?

options.A: Nurses can influence public policy and secure funding for community prevention programs
options.B: Nurses have the legal authority to pass national laws without legislative voting
options.C: Lawmakers only listen to nurses and ignore all other healthcare professionals
options.D: Advocacy replaces the need for direct clinical care in hospitals

explanation: Nurses use their frontline experience and health data to convince leaders to invest resources into preventive mental health initiatives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h8)

question: What does it usually mean if a baby's weight line drops downwards across percentiles on a growth chart?

options.A: Rapid acceleration of normal muscle mass
options.B: A normal growth spurt following a brief illness
options.C: Potential nutritional deficit or underlying health problem
options.D: An error in the initial recording of the birth weight

explanation: Spot on! A downward drop in weight percentiles is a warning sign that the baby might be falling behind due to illness or poor feeding. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T2#GNS225_U3_T2_h5)

question: Which statement best describes the role of most microorganisms found in food?

options.A: They always cause severe food poisoning if ingested raw
options.B: They are exclusively viruses that destroy plant cell walls
options.C: They are either harmless or beneficial rather than disease-causing
options.D: They have no effect on the nutritional value of food

explanation: While pathogenic microbes get a lot of attention, the majority of microorganisms in food do not cause disease and are often useful. [learn more](GST114_U3_T5#GST114_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is a major infrastructure barrier to EHR implementation in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Frequent power outages and unstable internet connectivity
options.B: Laws that strictly forbid the use of computers in medicine
options.C: Excessive availability of free software for every clinic
options.D: A complete lack of sick patients needing documentation

explanation: Unreliable power supply and poor internet access pose significant daily challenges to maintaining continuous digital health records in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T2#GNS113_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why do experts now believe the cerebellum is also involved in mental tasks, not just physical movement?

options.A: It stores all semantic memory traces gathered during childhood
options.B: It produces the majority of dopamine used in the frontal lobes
options.C: It generates conscious thoughts independently of the cerebral cortex
options.D: It maintains extensive neural loops connecting with prefrontal and limbic brain regions

explanation: The cerebellum doesn't just talk to motor areas; it connects with thinking and emotional centers too, helping influence our mood, memory, and language! Fascinating, right? [learn more](GNS211_U3_T22#GNS211_U3_T22_h5)

question: Why should nurses actively ask patients about their mood instead of waiting for them to bring it up?

options.A: Patients with depression lose the ability to speak completely
options.B: Hospital policy forbids patients from mentioning sadness first
options.C: Many patients keep feelings hidden due to social stigma
options.D: Physical assessments replace the need for verbal interviews

explanation: Spot on! Because society often judges mental health issues, many patients hide their pain. Asking gently and directly lets them know it's safe to talk. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T2#GNS324_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following is classified as pathological waste?

options.A: Used paper hand towels
options.B: Broken mercury thermometers
options.C: Surgically removed human tissues
options.D: Expired paracetamol tablets

explanation: Pathological waste specifically includes human tissues, organs, and body parts removed during surgeries or autopsies. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h2)

question: A nurse wants to publish a study, but she is nervous about criticism and lacks writing experience. What is her best first step?

options.A: Pay for expensive advertising space in a national newspaper
options.B: Wait until retirement to think about sharing study findings
options.C: Collaborate with an experienced mentor for guidance and support
options.D: Hide the research data inside a private bedside locker

explanation: Exactly! Working alongside an experienced mentor helps build your confidence, polish your writing, and calm those nerves. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h6)

question: Under Nigerian law, what is the main legal ground that allows for a safe and lawful termination of pregnancy?

options.A: When the pregnancy results from consensual sex
options.B: Upon the request of both parents
options.C: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.D: In cases of severe economic hardship

explanation: You've got this! Nigerian law is very strict, allowing pregnancy termination only when it is necessary to preserve the mother's life. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T023#GNS226_U5_T023_h1)

question: What is the main health benefit of early breast milk (colostrum) for a newborn?

options.A: It gives them high dietary fiber
options.B: It stops jaundice from happening
options.C: It acts as a sleeping pill
options.D: It provides heavy antibodies and protein to protect the tummy

explanation: Colostrum is liquid gold! It is packed with protective antibodies (like IgA) that line the baby's gut to fight off early germs. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T011#GNS226_U1_T011_h6)

question: When does the highest risk for postpartum hemorrhage and maternal death happen?

options.A: During the fourth month after delivery
options.B: Within the first 48 hours after childbirth
options.C: Two weeks before labor starts
options.D: At the final six-week checkup

explanation: That's right! The first 48 hours after birth are the most critical window for watching out for sudden, dangerous bleeding and infections. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h6)

question: What are the three main signs of professional burnout in healthcare workers?

options.A: Physical injury, financial debt, and lack of clinical qualifications
options.B: Fear of injections, poor handwriting, and slow documentation speed
options.C: Emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment
options.D: Chronic insomnia, sudden weight gain, and acute respiratory infections

explanation: Burnout hits hard in three ways: feeling totally drained, starting to treat patients coldly like objects, and feeling like your work doesn't matter anymore. [learn more](GST321_U3_T6#GST321_U3_T6_h6)

question: What is the primary role of skeletal muscles during ambulation?

options.A: Contracting to pull bones and create motion
options.B: Sending electrical signals to the brain
options.C: Producing red blood cells for oxygen transport
options.D: Absorbing shock within the joint spaces

explanation: Skeletal muscles shorten and pull on bones across joints to move the body forward during walking. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T8#GNS324_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which quick check do nurses use to spot life-threatening conditions in disaster victims first?

options.A: GCS neurological scale
options.B: Braden skin assessment
options.C: APGAR scoring system
options.D: ABCDE framework

explanation: Airway, Breathing, Circulation, Disability, and Exposure give us a fast, life-saving checklist in any emergency. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h6)

question: What are the three essential parts of a strong advocacy message?

options.A: The history, the theory, and the research
options.B: The problem, the solution, and the urgency
options.C: The budget, the timeline, and the penalty
options.D: The diagnosis, the drug, and the dosage

explanation: Keep it simple and clear: state what is broken, how to fix it, and why we need to act right now! [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h3)

question: Why must dangerous infections like cholera or yellow fever be classified as notifiable diseases?

options.A: To ensure that pharmaceutical companies make a profit on drugs
options.B: To prevent the affected patient from leaving their home ever again
options.C: To collect extra tax revenue from local healthcare facilities
options.D: To alert health authorities quickly so they can prevent a wider outbreak

explanation: You're right! Mandatory reporting allows public health teams to step in immediately and control transmission before it gets out of hand. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T90#GNS214_U1_T90_h5)

question: When listening to music, what property of a sound wave tells you whether the note is high or low (pitch)?

options.A: Resonance
options.B: Frequency
options.C: Amplitude
options.D: Velocity

explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz and determines the pitch of a sound. Think of high-frequency sounds as high-pitched, like a baby crying, and low-frequency as deep, like a drum! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T7#GNS211_U4_T7_h1)

question: What is the main difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation separates sick people, while quarantine separates exposed healthy people
options.B: Isolation is for bacterial infections, while quarantine is for viral diseases
options.C: Quarantine lasts for one year, while isolation lasts for only two hours
options.D: Quarantine is done in a hospital, while isolation is always done in a market

explanation: Easy way to remember: Isolation is for those who are already sick, while quarantine is for healthy people who were exposed and need to wait out the incubation period. [learn more](GST114_U2_T18#GST114_U2_T18_h5)

question: When must a nurse researcher use non-parametric statistical tests?

options.A: When the research study is funded by a government hospital
options.B: When the data does not follow a normal bell curve distribution
options.C: When the sample size is extremely large and perfectly random
options.D: When all study variables are measured on a continuous scale

explanation: Brilliant! If your data is messy or skewed and doesn't fit that neat bell-shaped curve, non-parametric tests save the day. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T3#GNS217_U4_T3_h7)

question: Why is building strong community resilience a vital part of disaster management?

options.A: Local populations are always the first responders before official help arrives
options.B: It eliminates the need for government funding during major crises
options.C: Villagers are legally required to purchase their own emergency ambulances
options.D: Community members can completely replace professional doctors and nurses

explanation: Local people are always on the ground first. Preparing them means lives can be saved immediately while waiting for external help. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T8#GNS315_U5_T8_h8)

question: Which of these statements about nursing leadership is FALSE?

options.A: It is built by taking on small projects and precepting students.
options.B: It is a continuous developmental journey throughout a career.
options.C: It can be cultivated through mentorship and continuing education.
options.D: It is an innate trait that cannot be learned or improved over time.

explanation: Leadership isn't a rare magic power you are born with! Anyone can grow and improve their leadership skills over time through practice, learning, and good mentors. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h8)

question: What is the purpose of the 'teach-back' method in home care?

options.A: Allowing the nurse to grade the family's cleaning skills
options.B: Checking if the patient or caregiver truly understands instructions
options.C: Testing the patient's ability to read a textbook out loud
options.D: Teaching the nurse how to use home appliances

explanation: Instead of asking 'Do you understand?', you ask them to explain the instructions back to you in their own words. It's a game-changer for safety! [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of patient categorization in home health care?

options.A: To group individuals based on their specific health needs and care type
options.B: To eliminate the need for home visits by professional nurses
options.C: To decide which patients must return to the hospital immediately
options.D: To reduce the total number of medications a patient takes daily

explanation: Categorizing patients allows nurses to understand unique care requirements and plan appropriate interventions for each person. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why do TB patients have to take a combination of multiple drugs instead of just one?

options.A: To prevent the patient from experiencing any side effects
options.B: To shorten the entire treatment course to one week
options.C: To prevent the development of drug-resistant bacterial strains
options.D: To make the medication taste better for the patient

explanation: Using a mix of drugs stops the sneaky TB germs from mutating and becoming resistant to treatment. Great nursing insight! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T6#GNS223_U2_T6_h1)

question: Where is the cell body of a preganglionic neuron located?

options.A: Target effector organ
options.B: Skeletal muscle fiber
options.C: Peripheral autonomic ganglion
options.D: Brain or spinal cord

explanation: Preganglionic neurons always originate inside the central nervous system, which includes the brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T29#GNS211_U3_T29_h3)

question: A patient becomes dizzy and nauseated shortly after taking a sublingual tablet. What unique advantage of this route can the nurse utilize?

options.A: Give a large glass of milk to neutralize the medicine.
options.B: Instruct the patient to spit out any remaining undissolved medication.
options.C: Wait for the liver to filter out the toxic portion.
options.D: Pump the patient's stomach immediately to remove the drug.

explanation: Because absorption happens in the mouth, removing unabsorbed medication can stop further entry into the blood. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h4)

question: A mother asks if she should give her four-month-old plain water on a very hot afternoon. What is the best response?

options.A: Give small amounts of boiled water between feedings
options.B: Replace one milk feeding with water to cool the baby
options.C: Breast milk or formula already provides enough hydration
options.D: Add sugar to the water to prevent low blood sugar

explanation: You nailed it! Babies under six months don't need extra water. Breast milk or formula has all the fluid they need, even when the weather is hot. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h3)

question: How long must continuous seizure activity last to be clinically defined as status epilepticus?

options.A: More than twenty-four hours
options.B: Longer than five minutes
options.C: At least one full hour
options.D: Exactly thirty seconds

explanation: Status epilepticus is defined as a seizure lasting more than five minutes or recurrent seizures without recovery of consciousness. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h7)

question: How do the kidneys respond when a patient develops metabolic acidosis?

options.A: They excrete more hydrogen ions and reabsorb bicarbonate
options.B: They reabsorb more hydrogen ions and excrete bicarbonate
options.C: They convert excess acid into glucose in the cortex
options.D: They stop all filtration until blood pH normalizes

explanation: To raise blood pH back to normal, the kidneys get rid of excess acid and keep bicarbonate to buffer the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h5)

question: Why is decontamination of chemical spill victims done outside the main hospital doors?

options.A: To make sure patients are completely dry before filling out admission paperwork
options.B: To allow emergency vehicles to park directly inside the treatment rooms
options.C: To comply with fire safety regulations regarding indoor water usage
options.D: To stop toxic substances from entering the hospital and harming staff and patients

explanation: Spot on! Cleaning patients outside keeps toxic fumes and chemicals from spreading inside and endangering everyone in the building. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h6)

question: How do enteric fevers primarily spread from one person to another?

options.A: Airborne droplets
options.B: Direct skin contact
options.C: Fecal-oral route
options.D: Mosquito bites

explanation: Correct! It's all about hygiene—enteric fevers spread when contaminated food or water is ingested. Handwashing is your best nursing defense here! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T17#GNS313_U2_T17_h2)

question: What is the main job of the effector in a homeostatic loop?

options.A: To carry out the final response that alters the internal environment
options.B: To constantly measure the exact temperature of the skin
options.C: To process signals and decide if a change is dangerous
options.D: To store excess glucose until the body needs extra fuel

explanation: Great job! Effectors are the doers—like muscles or sweat glands—that take the instructions and actually fix the imbalance in the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which question represents the core mindset shift of trauma-informed care?

options.A: Why did you act this way?
options.B: What happened to you?
options.C: When will you get over this?
options.D: Who is to blame for this?

explanation: Trauma-informed care shifts the focus from judging a person's behavior to understanding the painful past experiences that caused it. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T7#GNS314_U1_T7_h5)

question: What main thing defines 'special groups' in community health?

options.A: Having a very high financial income
options.B: Belonging to a particular political party
options.C: Higher health risks and limited access to care
options.D: Living exclusively in capital cities

explanation: You nailed it! Special groups are populations that face higher health vulnerabilities and struggle more to get standard healthcare. Knowing who they are helps us direct our care where it's needed most. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T26#GNS225_U5_T26_h1)

question: What is breakthrough pain?

options.A: Chronic pain that has permanently stopped responding to strong opioids
options.B: A sudden flare of severe discomfort that breaks through baseline medication
options.C: Mild discomfort that occurs only when the patient tries to stand up
options.D: The very first episode of pain a patient feels after surgery

explanation: Breakthrough pain is a temporary, sharp increase in intensity that occurs over a baseline of otherwise controlled discomfort. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h6)

question: Which of these is a major factor that restricts healthcare supply?

options.A: Excessive amounts of idle medical equipment in storage
options.B: An absolute absence of government regulations in hospitals
options.C: Low costs associated with purchasing new pharmaceuticals
options.D: Shortages of qualified nursing workforce and clinical staff

explanation: Right! Even if a ward has empty beds, a shortage of trained nurses and doctors means the hospital cannot safely take in more patients. [learn more](GST322_U1_T2#GST322_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the primary goal of drug information in nursing practice?

options.A: To promote safe and effective medication use
options.B: To eliminate the need for pharmacology textbooks
options.C: To replace the clinical judgment of physicians
options.D: To speed up the hospital discharge process

explanation: Drug information exists to ensure medications are used safely and correctly to benefit the patient. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T3#GNS215_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why does a lack of dystrophin cause muscle damage in Duchenne muscular dystrophy?

options.A: The muscle cell membrane becomes fragile and tears during normal contractions.
options.B: The muscle cells lose their ability to receive nerve impulses from the spinal cord.
options.C: Satellite cells multiply too quickly and crowd out functional muscle tissue.
options.D: Calcium builds up in the cell and immediately dissolves the bones.

explanation: Without dystrophin to absorb the shock, the outer membrane of the muscle cell easily tears every time the muscle contracts. You're building solid clinical knowledge! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T8#GNS121_U3_T8_h6)

question: What should you do with a surgical instrument that has a broken ratchet during inspection?

options.A: Removed from circulation immediately
options.B: Stored in the sterile room for minor procedures
options.C: Sent straight to the sterilization autoclave
options.D: Wrapped tightly in a double linen layer

explanation: You got it! Damaged tools won't work right during surgery and tiny cracks can hide bacteria. Pull them out of use right away. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why is pushing down on top of the mother's bump (fundal pressure) a big no-no during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: It stops the placenta from delivering after the baby
options.B: It makes the baby turn around into a breech position
options.C: It causes the mother's blood pressure to drop too low
options.D: It can cause the trapped shoulder to wedge tighter and rupture the uterus

explanation: Pushing from above only jams the shoulder harder against the bone. Avoid fundal pressure completely in shoulder dystocia! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h5)

question: What does 'voluntary participation' mean when recruiting study participants?

options.A: Participants must be paid a large cash reward for joining the study
options.B: Patients must complete all questionnaires before leaving the hospital ward
options.C: Hospital management decides which patients are best suited for the study
options.D: Patients can choose to join or refuse without facing any negative consequences

explanation: Brilliant! Participation must always be completely free choice—no penalties, no pressure. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h7)

question: Why is it important to ask if a patient's joint pain started suddenly after an accident or came on slowly?

options.A: It helps differentiate between acute traumatic injuries and chronic degenerative diseases
options.B: It measures the patient's baseline daily fluid intake
options.C: It proves whether the patient requires emergency psychological counseling
options.D: It indicates the exact blood pressure medication the patient needs

explanation: You nailed it. Sudden pain usually points to trauma like a fall, while slow pain often means wear-and-tear or arthritis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T2#GNS222_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which chemical builds up in your brain throughout the day to make you feel sleepy?

options.A: Melatonin
options.B: Adenosine
options.C: Acetylcholine
options.D: Cortisol

explanation: Adenosine piles up the longer you stay awake, creating sleep pressure until you finally rest and clear it out. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h6)

question: Which family planning supply method gives dual protection against BOTH pregnancy and sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Male condoms
options.B: Oral contraceptive pills
options.C: Spermicidal creams
options.D: Cervical caps

explanation: Condoms act as a physical shield that blocks body fluids, stopping both conception and many infections at once. Smart nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T5#GNS225_U3_T5_h2)

question: Which serious infection can easily spread by sharing unsterilized blades during scarification?

options.A: Typhoid fever
options.B: Common malaria
options.C: Hepatitis B
options.D: Simple cholera

explanation: Exactly! Unclean cutting tools transfer blood-borne viruses like Hepatitis B and HIV directly from person to person. Safety first! [learn more](GNS225_U6_T7#GNS225_U6_T7_h3)

question: Which medication is absolutely essential for a patient living with Type 1 diabetes to survive?

options.A: Metformin
options.B: Acarbose
options.C: Sulfonylurea
options.D: Insulin

explanation: Because Type 1 bodies cannot make insulin, daily insulin replacement is a matter of survival. Another win for your clinical knowledge today! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h4)

question: How does delaying salary payments during economic hardships affect nurses?

options.A: They have no impact on daily clinical performance
options.B: They encourage nurses to work longer hours with enthusiasm
options.C: They improve interprofessional collaboration within the ward
options.D: They demotivate staff and can trigger industrial strikes

explanation: Unpaid salaries cause real financial stress, lowering morale and sometimes leading to strikes as workers demand what is due. [learn more](GST322_U3_T5#GST322_U3_T5_h6)

question: A nurse in a clinic after a severe flood is busy checking water supplies and looking out for skin rashes. What phase of disaster care is this?

options.A: Pre-disaster planning
options.B: Emergency architectural damage assessment
options.C: Recovery and stopping secondary disease outbreaks
options.D: Immediate search and rescue operations

explanation: Watching water and skin health after a flood helps catch and stop fresh infections while the community heals. Brilliant work today! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T11#GNS315_U1_T11_h5)

question: Who is the focus of medical isolation compared to quarantine?

options.A: Travelers arriving from a foreign country
options.B: People who are currently sick with an infection
options.C: Healthcare workers who finished their shift
options.D: Healthy family members of a sick patient

explanation: Isolation separates individuals who already have a confirmed or suspected active infection from others. [learn more](GST114_U2_T16#GST114_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is a major financial headache caused by unreliable public electricity in Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Automatic shutdown of all nursing schools
options.B: Heavy financial expenditure on diesel generators
options.C: Immediate reduction in patient admission rates
options.D: Instant conversion of hospitals to digital clinics

explanation: Spot on! Hospitals have to spend a massive chunk of their budgets buying diesel just to keep emergency lights and life-saving machines running. [learn more](GST322_U3_T4#GST322_U3_T4_h5)

question: How is nursing counselling different from a standard health interview?

options.A: Counselling focuses on emotional support and coping
options.B: Counselling relies exclusively on closed-ended questions
options.C: Counselling replaces all physical health assessments
options.D: Counselling is only performed by hospital chaplains

explanation: Great thinking! While an interview gathers facts, counselling helps patients process feelings and handle health challenges. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h1)

question: Why does the outer layer of the skin (epidermis) have to rely on diffusion to get its nutrients?

options.A: It is made entirely of dead cells.
options.B: It repels blood vessels using keratin.
options.C: It is too thick for capillaries to enter.
options.D: It lacks a direct blood supply.

explanation: Exactly! The epidermis doesn't have its own blood vessels (it's avascular). Because of this, nutrients have to quietly seep up from the dermis living right below it. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T2#GNS211_U2_T2_h2)

question: How should a nurse handle bed sheets that are stained with blood?

options.A: Handle them with minimal agitation and bag them securely
options.B: Wash them by hand in the patient bathroom sink
options.C: Leave them on the floor until housekeeping arrives
options.D: Shake them out thoroughly to remove loose debris

explanation: You nailed it! Shaking dirty linens sends dust and germs flying everywhere. Roll them up gently and bag them safely! [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: A patient is having a full panic attack due to a phobia. What should be the nurse's very first priority?

options.A: Leave the patient alone so they can calm down in private
options.B: Force the patient to face the fear source immediately
options.C: Help the patient feel safe and lower immediate anxiety
options.D: Teach complex problem-solving skills during the peak of panic

explanation: When panic peaks, keep it simple. Stay calm, be present, and focus on helping them feel secure until the storm passes. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T6#GNS314_U2_T6_h6)

question: Why do many maternal deaths that happen outside of hospitals fail to show up in official government records?

options.A: The government automatically investigates and solves every home death.
options.B: International health agencies ban rural home deaths from being counted.
options.C: They happen at home and are never recorded by a formal civil registration system.
options.D: Traditional attendants are legally required to publish daily newspaper logs.

explanation: Without strong local registration or mandatory reporting for home deliveries, deaths happening in rural communities sadly remain invisible to official tallies. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h6)

question: A patient eats plenty of carbs but lacks B-complex vitamins. What is likely to happen?

options.A: Cells struggle to release energy from those carbohydrates
options.B: The kidneys start filtering out all the extra glucose
options.C: The patient instantly develops severe muscle wasting
options.D: Blood sugar levels drop to zero within a few minutes

explanation: Exactly! Without B-vitamins acting as helpers, your cells have a hard time unlocking the energy trapped inside the food you eat. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T013#GNS227_U1_T013_h4)

question: Why must you store your interview audio files and transcripts in password-protected digital folders?

options.A: To prevent accidental loss of data and protect patient confidentiality
options.B: To speed up the internet connection in the research office
options.C: To make the files look more professional for publishing
options.D: To allow the general public to read private hospital stories

explanation: Exactly right! Patient stories are deeply personal, and keeping digital files secure is a core part of ethical nursing practice. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T24#GNS224_U1_T24_h7)

question: A nurse opens a sterile dressing pack for a patient, but the procedure is cancelled before the pack is touched. What is the best nursing action to minimize waste?

options.A: Place the pack in the general waste bin to save space
options.B: Check hospital policy to see if the unopened sterile pack remains usable
options.C: Send the pack immediately to the hospital incinerator
options.D: Throw the unopened pack straight into the infectious waste bin

explanation: If a sterile barrier is completely intact and unopened, facility guidelines often allow it to remain sterile, preventing needless waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T12#GST114_U6_T12_h3)

question: Which chart type is best for showing how a clinical metric changes over time?

options.A: Scatter plot
options.B: Bar chart
options.C: Pie chart
options.D: Line graph

explanation: Correct! Line graphs connect dots over time, making them perfect for watching trends across weeks or months. [learn more](GST319_U1_T2#GST319_U1_T2_h4)

question: What happens at the pyramidal decussation in the medulla oblongata?

options.A: Motor fibers cross over to the opposite side
options.B: Cranial nerve nuclei merge into a single structure
options.C: Oxygen exchange occurs for brain tissue
options.D: Cerebrospinal fluid is filtered out of the blood

explanation: Decussation is just a fancy word for crossing over! Here, most of the motor pathways cross to the opposite side of the body, which is why the left brain controls the right side of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T18#GNS211_U3_T18_h3)

question: What happens when you take in more food energy (calories) than your body burns off?

options.A: Excess energy is stored primarily as fat
options.B: The body uses up its protein stores completely
options.C: Cellular chemical reactions stop entirely
options.D: Metabolic rate drops permanently to zero

explanation: Think of it like money: if you earn more than you spend, you save the extra! The body packs away extra calories as fat tissue to use for a rainy day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T014#GNS227_U1_T014_h1)

question: What common emotional challenge do family caregivers often face when a patient returns home on leave?

options.A: High levels of anxiety and fear regarding potential relapse
options.B: Excessive anger because the hospital cures patients too quickly
options.C: Confusion caused by sudden physical weight gain
options.D: Complete boredom due to the patient's lack of needs

explanation: It's completely normal for families to feel anxious and worry about handling unexpected symptom flare-ups at home. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T6#GNS314_U5_T6_h5)

question: What report should a nurse fill out right away after a medication near-miss or error?

options.A: Discharge summary report
options.B: Financial audit report
options.C: Public health census report
options.D: Incident report

explanation: Incident reports let the hospital look at safety issues objectively so they can prevent the same thing from happening again. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T7#GNS113_U2_T7_h5)

question: What exactly is a 'referral feedback loop'?

options.A: A phone call from the ministry of health checking staff attendance
options.B: The routine cleaning schedule of the primary healthcare ambulance
options.C: Information sent back from the receiving hospital to the referring clinic
options.D: A complaint made by a patient about long hospital queues

explanation: You're doing great! The feedback loop simply means the big hospital sends information back to let your clinic know what happened to the patient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h6)

question: How should a nurse document anatomical findings related to FGM in a patient's chart?

options.A: Omitting the findings entirely to protect patient privacy
options.B: Using local slang terms to help other nurses understand
options.C: Describing the family as criminal in the nursing notes
options.D: Using respectful, objective, and standard clinical terminology

explanation: Correct! Always use professional, non-judgmental language that describes the physical findings accurately without shaming the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T8#GNS312_U1_T8_h3)

question: A nurse sorts patients by their blood groups (A, B, AB, or O). What level of measurement is this?

options.A: Ratio
options.B: Ordinal
options.C: Nominal
options.D: Interval

explanation: Spot on! Blood groups are just names or categories with no numerical value or rank. Whenever you're just labeling categories, it's nominal data. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h2)

question: What do we call the signs of pregnancy that are felt and reported only by the mother herself?

options.A: Diagnostic signs
options.B: Presumptive signs
options.C: Probable signs
options.D: Positive signs

explanation: You've got this! Presumptive signs are subjective changes the mother experiences firsthand, like missed periods or sore breasts. Think of them as clues she notices herself. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T002#GNS226_U2_T002_h1)

question: Can an overweight patient still suffer from poor nutrition? If so, why?

options.A: Yes, because body weight doesn't show the quality of micronutrients consumed
options.B: Yes, because overweight people cannot absorb proteins at all
options.C: No, because excess body fat stores all necessary vitamins forever
options.D: No, because larger people always have fast metabolisms

explanation: A person can eat plenty of calories and still lack essential vitamins and minerals. That's hidden malnutrition! [learn more](GNS227_U5_T004#GNS227_U5_T004_h1)

question: Why is addressing psychosocial issues important alongside physical pain management?

options.A: It guarantees a full recovery from the terminal condition
options.B: Patients only experience suffering in their minds
options.C: Terminal illness affects the whole person, not just the body
options.D: It replaces the need for any pharmaceutical pain relief

explanation: A serious illness disrupts a person's entire life experience, requiring care that reaches beyond physical symptoms. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h1)

question: What is the standard metric unit for measuring liquid volume in the ward?

options.A: Drop
options.B: Grain
options.C: Pound
options.D: Milliliter

explanation: Liters and milliliters (mL) are our go-to units for measuring liquid medications and IV fluids every day. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h3)

question: What must happen for a child to be born with sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Only the mother needs to have the full sickle cell disease
options.B: The child must be exposed to severe malaria during infancy
options.C: Both parents must pass on a copy of the mutated sickle cell gene
options.D: Either parent must have genotype AS while the other has genotype AA

explanation: Because it is an autosomal recessive condition, a child needs two copies of the abnormal gene, requiring both parents to contribute a sickle gene. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T16#GNS214_U1_T16_h2)

question: A psychiatric nurse visits a client at home and notices early signs of a psychiatric relapse. What action should the nurse take first?

options.A: Advise the family to immediately lock the client inside a room until the mood passes
options.B: Review the current treatment plan, assess stressors, and collaborate with the multidisciplinary team
options.C: Wait for the client to come to the distant tertiary hospital next year
options.D: Discharge the client from the CBR program because treatment has failed

explanation: Early intervention involves assessing what triggered the relapse, adjusting support, and working with the team before full hospitalization becomes necessary. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T3#GNS314_U5_T3_h3)

question: How does time-driven activity-based costing make hospital budgeting better?

options.A: By calculating costs strictly at the end of each fiscal year
options.B: By measuring the exact time spent on specific clinical activities
options.C: By ignoring staff salaries and focusing only on medical equipment
options.D: By assuming all hospital stays cost the exact same amount

explanation: This method looks at how many minutes tasks actually take, giving a super accurate picture of what care really costs. [learn more](GST322_U2_T3#GST322_U2_T3_h5)

question: When are your kidneys most likely to start producing extra glucose?

options.A: Prolonged fasting or starvation
options.B: Excessive intake of dietary water
options.C: A sudden spike in blood pressure
options.D: Eating a large carbohydrate-rich meal

explanation: Exactly right! When liver energy stores run out during a long fast, the kidneys step up and make glucose to help keep your body fueled. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T7#GNS121_U2_T7_h8)

question: Which complication is a major risk for patients who have to stay in bed for a long time?

options.A: Pressure injuries
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Deafness
options.D: Hyperglycemia

explanation: Spot on! Staying in one position cuts off blood flow over bony areas, making skin breakdown a huge risk. That's why turning patients regularly is so important! [learn more](GST319_U4_T7#GST319_U4_T7_h2)

question: What is always the very first step in the community health planning cycle?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Implementation
options.D: Budgeting

explanation: Spot on! Before you can help or build a program, you first need to assess and understand what is going on in the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T19#GNS225_U2_T19_h2)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for during patient handovers?

options.A: System, Bedside, Assessment, Report
options.B: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Action, Recovery
options.C: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.D: Safety, Breathing, Airway, Resuscitation

explanation: Spot on! SBAR helps you give a quick, clear, and structured update whenever you are handing over a patient to another nurse or doctor. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why is good record-keeping at the triage desk so important for legal safety?

options.A: It stops patients from asking questions about their treatment costs

options.C: It guarantees the hospital will win any lawsuit brought by insurance companies
options.D: It allows nurses to avoid writing shift reports at the end of the day

explanation: Clear notes prove exactly when the patient came in and how you cared for them. Good documentation is your best legal shield! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T1#GNS315_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why does the center of a developing cartilage model start to calcify?

options.A: Chondrocytes hypertrophy and restrict nutrient diffusion through the matrix
options.B: Synovial fluid leaks into the center of the shaft
options.C: Local nerve endings stimulate mineral crystallization

question: Why must a nurse flush a feeding tube before and after giving medication or formula?

options.A: To cool down the internal stomach lining
options.B: To stimulate natural saliva production
options.C: To prevent the tube from clogging
options.D: To increase the patient's daily water weight

explanation: Feeding tubes are narrow and can easily block up with thick formula or crushed meds. A simple water flush keeps everything flowing smoothly. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h5)

question: Why should digital health training be part of nursing education?

options.A: To prepare students for tech-driven healthcare environments
options.B: To replace clinical hospital practice with computer games
options.C: To ensure nurses never have to speak to patients in person
options.D: To make nursing school programs shorter and easier

explanation: Spot on! Healthcare is evolving with technology, and learning these skills early sets you up for success in the modern field. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h8)

question: What is preventable harm in healthcare?

options.A: Allergic reactions to drugs with no prior history of allergy
options.B: Unavoidable side effects of a necessary surgical operation
options.C: Natural progression of a terminal disease without treatment
options.D: Damage caused by failing to follow accepted standards of care

explanation: Preventable harm is injury that could have been avoided if standard safety practices were properly followed. Every check we do counts! [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which group of hormones is made directly from cholesterol?

options.A: Amine hormones
options.B: Steroid hormones
options.C: Peptide hormones
options.D: Protein hormones

question: If a nurse researcher tests patients with a pain scale twice, why is a very short time interval between tests sometimes a bad idea?

options.A: The patients will experience severe physical exhaustion
options.B: Hospital management will not approve the extra paperwork
options.C: Patients might remember and repeat their previous answers
options.D: The thermometer or scale will lose its electrical charge

explanation: This is called recall bias! If patients just remember what they wrote five minutes ago, they'll copy it, making the tool look more reliable than it actually is. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h3)

question: A patient recovering from an intentional overdose is now awake and stable. What nursing action is most important?

options.A: Restricting all family visits to punish the patient for the suicide attempt
options.B: Providing continuous observation and psychological support while keeping the environment safe
options.C: Avoiding any conversation about the incident to prevent embarrassment
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately with a prescription for sedatives

explanation: You've got this. Emotional support and a safe, watch-careful environment are vital for anyone recovering from self-harm. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T14#GNS221_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is expected of a nurse operating under emergency laws or Good Samaritan rules during a disaster?

options.A: To perform complex surgical procedures outside their normal training
options.B: To act in good faith and stay within their training and scope of practice
options.C: To prioritize personal safety above all community rescue operations
options.D: To completely disregard documentation and patient safety guidelines

explanation: Emergency laws protect you when you help out, as long as you do your best and stay within what you've been trained to do as a nurse. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h8)

question: What is the medical term for coughing up blood-stained sputum?

options.A: Hemoptysis
options.B: Melena
options.C: Hematemesis
options.D: Epistaxis

question: How does scarcity directly affect your daily life as a nurse on the ward?

options.A: It forces nurses to prioritize care and manage limited supplies efficiently

options.C: It automatically lowers the quality of medications available in pharmacies
options.D: It prevents hospitals from ever admitting emergency trauma patients

explanation: Spot on! Because time and gloves are never endless, great nurses learn to prioritize and manage what they have to keep every patient safe. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h1)

question: What fields are combined in nursing informatics?

options.A: Pharmacology, anatomy, and clinical psychology
options.B: Public health, epidemiology, and health economics
options.C: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.D: Biology, chemistry, and hospital administration

explanation: Nursing informatics merges nursing principles with computer and information technology to improve data management and patient care outcomes. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient has high IgG levels against a virus, but feels totally fine with normal lab results. What does this usually mean?

options.C: An active parasite infestation in the gastrointestinal tract
options.D: An acute, life-threatening infection requiring immediate isolation

explanation: Having IgG around long-term is a good thing! It shows your immune system has a memory bank from a previous infection or a vaccine, not a current sickness. [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h6)

question: Early in your research journey, how does having a theoretical framework help you?

options.A: Clear research questions
options.B: The hospital budget
options.C: The nursing shift schedule
options.D: Patient discharge summaries

explanation: Well done! A good framework shines a light on what you need to study, making it much easier to write sharp and focused research questions. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T12#GNS217_U3_T12_h3)

question: Which agency sets and enforces the main federal regulations for skilled nursing facilities?

options.A: Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA)
options.B: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
options.C: World Health Organization (WHO)
options.D: National Institutes of Health (NIH)

explanation: CMS oversees the federal rules and quality standards that certified skilled nursing facilities must follow. You're building a strong regulatory foundation! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T11#GNS324_U5_T11_h8)

question: What does human factors engineering mainly look at in a hospital setting?

options.A: The psychological mental health disorders of incoming hospital patients
options.B: How humans interact with equipment, tools, and working environments
options.C: The financial cost of hiring nursing staff for night shift duties
options.D: How physical exercise improves the cardiovascular health of nurses

explanation: Human factors look at how well our tools and workspaces fit our daily tasks, helping us design environments where mistakes are harder to make. [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which nutritional shortage is most commonly linked to tiredness and poor school performance in teenagers?

options.A: Iron deficiency anemia

options.D: Vitamin C toxicity

question: What does 'organisational culture' mean in a hospital or clinic?

options.A: The daily shift schedule assigned by the head nurse
options.B: The physical building layout and available medical equipment
options.C: The written disciplinary policies enforced by human resources
options.D: The shared values and unspoken rules that guide staff behaviour

explanation: Spot on! Culture is all about the invisible norms, habits, and attitudes that shape how work actually gets done on the ward every day. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h1)

question: A midwife wants to gain the trust of a conservative community before introducing family planning education. What is the best initial step?

options.C: Demand that the village chief close down all local shrines
options.D: Threaten residents with withdrawal of all general healthcare

explanation: Building trust requires listening and showing respect for local culture before attempting to introduce sensitive health topics. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T018#GNS226_U5_T018_h6)

question: How does a flannel graph help you out during a community health talk?

options.B: By printing thousands of takeaway leaflets for mothers attending the clinic
options.C: By allowing the nurse to move felt illustrations on a board to tell an interactive story

explanation: Flannel graphs use fuzzy cut-outs that stick to a board. As you talk, you can move them around to build a fun, visual story with your audience! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why is checking the airway always the very first step in emergency care?

options.A: Hospital rules strictly say airway first
options.B: It keeps the patient from talking too much
options.C: A blocked airway can cause death in minutes
options.D: It is the easiest thing to do in a busy ward

explanation: Spot on! Without a clear airway, oxygen can't reach the lungs, leading to brain death and cardiac arrest very fast. Airway always comes first! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is a common mistake school administrators make when it comes to health policies?

options.A: Allowing students to write their own safety rules
options.B: Consulting too many medical professionals before acting
options.C: Making policies that are far too simple to understand
options.D: Drafting policies but failing to actually enforce them

explanation: That's right. Writing a great policy on paper won't help if management doesn't follow through and monitor it daily! [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h2)

question: The QA committee notices nurses are struggling with children's drug dosage calculations. What is the best step to take?

options.A: Wait until a patient gets harmed before taking action
options.B: Stop giving all drugs to children immediately
options.C: Suspend all nurses working in the children's ward
options.D: Organize training workshops and provide clear dosing charts

question: Aside from treating cuts and bruises, what was another big focus for early industrial nurses?

options.C: Designing safer mechanical looms and steam engines for factory floors

question: Why do people often compare a research design to an architect's drawing?

options.C: It is only created by engineers rather than healthcare workers
options.D: It is drawn on large blueprint paper using physical ink

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure two hours after giving a BP medication to see if it worked. Which phase of the nursing process is this?

options.D: Diagnosis

question: Which urethral sphincter can you consciously control using your skeletal muscles?

options.D: External urethral sphincter

question: Which drug do you keep on hand to reverse breathing difficulties in a newborn whose mother received strong pain meds during labor?

options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Atropine

question: Why do search engines use an index instead of reading every document from scratch every time?

options.C: To make the search process happen almost instantly
options.D: To permanently delete outdated nursing research articles

question: How do we tell an indirect obstetric cause of maternal death apart from a direct one?

options.A: It has no relation to the female reproductive system at all

options.C: It is exclusively caused by surgical errors
options.D: It is caused by a pre-existing medical condition worsened by pregnancy

explanation: Spot on! Indirect causes are medical issues like heart disease or severe malaria that were already there, but got dangerously worse because of the physical changes of pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T014#GNS226_U1_T014_h4)

question: A colleague asks to quickly log in under your computer account because they forgot their password. What should you do?

options.A: Complete the charting for them under your own name instead
options.B: Refuse and ask them to log in using their own credentials
options.C: Allow them to type quickly while you watch over their shoulder
options.D: Write your password down on a sticky note for them to use later

question: Why is it so important to check how a patient is feeling emotionally before teaching them about their medications?

options.A: Patients who are afraid will refuse to answer demographic survey questions
options.B: Fear and anxiety can prevent the patient from retaining instructions
options.C: Emotional distress changes the chemical makeup of oral medications

question: Why is that long plateau phase so important for the heart?
